title: Survive dead-browser canary flakes without failing the whole gate
goal: PROBLEM: The canary E2E phase (playwright, retries: 0 in canary-e2e/playwright.config.js) fails the entire gate when 1-2 tests out of ~140 hit an infrastructure flake: 'page.goto: Target page, context or browser has been closed' inside waitForAppReady (canary-e2e/tests/helpers.js). The helper's single page.goto re-issue cannot recover when the whole browser/context died under gate-host load (it retries the navigation on the same dead page, so the retry line itself throws), and each red gate burns a ~17 minute canary run plus a full failback loop for the agent. FIX (pick the smallest robust option): when the retry also throws a browser-closed signature (has been closed / Target closed / Page crashed / ERR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES), recreate the browser context and re-issue once more; or mark exactly that signature as an infra-flake retried at the runner level / in a non-blocking quarantine lane with a recorded baseline. Genuine app failures (dead backend, bad URL, broken shell failing twice) must stay red. Document how to add signatures. ACCEPTANCE: (1) the browser-closed signature no longer fails the gate on its own; (2) a genuinely broken app shell still fails; (3) the CI report names which lane/signature was retried or quarantined. RELATED: task 8769b002 seeded a flaky-test quarantine with three other signatures; this signature is not covered and the helpers.js recovery gap is still present. CASE STUDY: KainBain task cf4b6847-11eb-4d59-b39e-e31b31df1150: 4 of its 5 Automated-tests cycles on 2026-11-19 failed on this identical signature (see automated-tests-failure-20261119-152819/160115/162951/170814.md tails, all at helpers.js:65, 139-140 passed with 1-2 flaked) while the ticket's own suites were green. See docs/tasks/cf4b6847-11eb-4d59-b39e-e31b31df1150/.

Read text file `docs/agent-docs/FLAKY_TEST_GUIDE.md`.
1|# Flaky-test prevention & diagnosis
2|
3|A test that passes *most* of the time is not a passing test — it is a failure
4|that hides. This repo runs its suites on a shared 4-core host under the
5|overlapped gate (`npm test` runs api + frontend + lint + build + scans in one
6|window), so a green run on an idle box is not evidence of stability. The
7|standard here is **a pass rate**, measured by repeating the suite.
8|
9|## Measuring a flake
10|
11|`scripts/repeat-tests.mjs` runs one suite (optionally filtered to one file)
12|`N` times and prints the per-run result plus the pass rate. Every run appends a
13|JSON object to a JSONL log under the OS temp dir and keeps the raw suite output
14|beside it, so a failing run's exact signature can be read afterwards.
15|
16|```bash
17|node scripts/repeat-tests.mjs --suite api      --pattern api/index.test.js --runs 10
18|node scripts/repeat-tests.mjs --suite frontend --pattern StageSkillsPanel   --runs 10
19|node scripts/repeat-tests.mjs --suite canary   --runs 3
20|```
21|
22|- `--suite api|frontend|canary` (default `api`), `--runs N` (default 5).
23|- `--pattern` is a file/name filter passed to the suite's own runner; a leading
24|  `api/` / `frontend/` prefix is stripped so `api/index.test.js` resolves in the
25|  `api` workspace.
26|- Logs land in `$TMPDIR/kainbain-flake-repeat/` (never committed).
27|- Exit code is `0` only when **every** run passed.
28|
29|Under load is the only honest stress: run the suspects while the full gate is
30|running, or on a constrained CPU set, e.g.
31|
32|```bash
33|npm test &                                             # the overlap window
34|taskset -c 0,1 node scripts/repeat-tests.mjs --suite frontend --pattern ObservabilityDashboard --runs 5
35|```
36|
37|A fix closes its audit row only on **100% green** — 10 standalone runs plus 3
38|under the overlapped gate. A fix that lowers the rate without zeroing it is not
39|done.
40|
41|## Checklist for writing a non-flaky test
42|
43|1. **Isolate state.** Never touch the live projects root or notes space — the
44|   `api/testSetup.isolation.js` throwaway roots are the backstop, and per-file
45|   suites mint their own pair via `isolatedTestRoots.js` + clean up in
46|   `afterAll`. Use `fs.mkdtemp` for scratch dirs. Never hard-code a
47|   projects/notes path.
48|2. **Isolate ports.** Bind ephemeral ports (`listen(0)`) or go through
49|   `scripts/free-port.mjs`. Never hard-code a listener port in a unit test.
50|3. **Wait for conditions, not sleeps.** Use `waitFor` / `findBy*` /
51|   `waitForElementToBeRemoved` (React) and Playwright's auto-retrying web-first
52|   assertions. A fixed `setTimeout` is both slower and flakier: it passes a real
53|   regression that fires later and fails under load. For API/flow tests use the
54|   existing `waitFor(condition, { timeoutMs })` polling helpers.
55|4. **Never assert wall-clock durations or random values.** Inject or fake the
56|   clock (`vi.useFakeTimers`, `vi.spyOn(Date, "now")`), seed or stub randomness.
57|   Performance-shape assertions must have a measured margin and a comment.
58|5. **Keep the async budget in step with the suite budget.** React Testing
59|   Library's `waitFor`/`findBy*` default to their own 1000ms
60|   (`asyncUtilTimeout`), *not* vitest's `testTimeout`. It is pinned in
61|   `frontend/src/setupTests.js` (guarded by
62|   `frontend/src/setupTests.asyncBudget.test.js`); if you add a suite that needs
63|   longer, raise it there once, not per file.
64|6. **Stay hermetic for network / CLI.** Mock harness (`KAINBAIN_DEFAULT_HARNESS=mock`),
65|   the agy fixture (`KAINBAIN_AGY_BIN`), and the `NODE_ENV=test` pin are the
66|   seams — no live fetches or real CLI spawns in unit tests.
67|7. **Pool-pinning rule (frontend).** A suite that needs node builtins must use
68|   the `node` environment or drop the api/node import (the
69|   `ObservabilityDashboard.session` precedent, asserted by the node-env contract
70|   in `tests/run-parallel.test.mjs`). Only a suite that is *proven* sensitive to
71|   `vmThreads` worker sharing may move to `legacy-pool` (forks) — and then both
72|   the `include` **and** the matching `main` project `exclude` must be added, or
73|   the suite runs twice / silently drops.
74|8. **Timeout raises need measured justification.** A raised `testTimeout` /
75|   `hookTimeout` must carry a comment with the measured overlap evidence (see
76|   the `OVERLAP_TIMEOUT_MS` notes in both `vitest.config.js` files).
77|9. **No retries to hide flakes.** Do not add global `retries` to vitest,
78|   and the canary suite runs with `retries: 0` — every flake fails the gate
79|   loudly, gets filed as a flake row, and gets fixed.
80|
81|## When you find a flake
82|
83|1. Record a row in the task's flake audit table: suite/file/test, failure
84|   signature, hit rate (`x/N`), class (timing / shared-state / port-file /
85|   clock / random / pool / network), and the fix.
86|2. Fix the **root cause** with the smallest change (usually test-only); if the
87|   fix must touch production code, call it out explicitly for review.
88|3. Prove it: repeat the fixed file 10× standalone **and** 3× under the
89|   overlapped gate; attach the JSONL log path to the row.
90|4. If the hit rate is 0/N after 10 standalone + 3 overlapped runs, deprioritise
91|   it with a note instead of changing it blind.

I read the task docs, the canary test helper, the Playwright config, and the case-study failure reports, then appended a new question round to the survey (round 1 from a previous attempt is preserved untouched; both JSON blocks validate).

**What I confirmed in the repo:** the app-loading helper today re-issues the page load only once and only on the *same* page, so when the whole browser dies under gate-host load the retry itself throws and the red gate is unrecoverable. The Playwright config deliberately sets `retries: 0`, the helper is called from ~25 spec files (~100 call sites), and the quarantine list seeded by task 8769b002 does not live in this repo.

**New questions for you (Round 2, now in `docs/tasks/44125086-d5aa-4bd3-a6c7-04eef809f59b/SURVEY.md`):**

1. **Spec-file changes** — the helper only receives the test's page; if the whole browser dies, a real fix must create a brand-new page. Are you OK changing the ~25 spec files, or must the recovery be hidden so no spec changes?
2. **Where the flake list lives** — should the official list of "known infra-flake" error messages be a committed data file next to the canary tests, live where task 8769b002 put its three signatures (tell me where), or sit inside the gate script?
3. **Scope of a gate-level retry** — when a failed test matches the flake list, is re-running just that test acceptable, or must the whole ~17-minute canary run repeat?
4. **Tracking** — should forgiven flakes be counted in a recorded baseline per signature so they can be removed later once proven fixed, or is a clear CI-report line naming the lane/signature enough?

(On top of the existing Round 1: which fix option to build, how much of the helper gets recovery, where the CI report must name the lane/signature, whether quarantined tests still run, and exactly which error messages count as "browser died".)
